_doc: Dress sheets for authored portraits (design/world/depth/art/README.md): one per sect or group, from the sect page's dress line. Inserted between the style block and the subject paragraph. Pilot: six sects; the rest are written with the batches. Rule (user 2026-11-25): cultivators are never poorly dressed; a humble sect is plain, not ragged.
bang_tam: Băng Tâm Các, an Ice sect of the frozen north: undyed white robes of fine cloth; inner disciples add a pale-blue sash, elders a sash of frost silk that looks cold; no bright colour anywhere; a faint rime on the cloth.
phat_y: Phất Y Cốc, hired swordsmen of a dry southern valley: well-cut robes of fine undyed grey cloth with one long left sleeve that hangs past the hand (outer disciples short sleeves); plain in colour but of excellent make, clean and pressed; a sword always close.
lac_ha: Lạc Hà Các, a sunset sect of the western islands and steppe: robes of sturdy hemp dyed with madder and steppe dust to the colours of evening; outer disciples pale ochre, inner rust, true disciples and elders dusk violet; small hall pins (a grey goose feather, a stern-lamp clasp, a pressed red maple leaf).
bach_vu: Bách Vũ Các, bird keepers of the jungle hills: cloaks sewn from moulted feathers of many browns and blues, leather gauntlets for the birds, practical jungle cloth beneath.
coc_vu: Cốc Vũ Quán, a rain-calling rice abbey: plain grey robes of good hemp-silk, neatly kilted to the knee for the terraces, clean and well kept; rice-straw hats; rain-callers wear fine black rain cloaks over the grey.
tung_dao: Tùng Đào Cung, the palace of the pine sea: robes of fine undyed pine-bark linen, soft and well tailored, hair pinned with a pine twig; inner disciples add a needle-green silk sash; elders wear grey-green.
